projects.name: The ovarian paper
projects.status: CDK4/6 inhibitor cocktail in ovarian cancer cells (HEYA8, SKOV3). Quiescence/EOC. **PAR = palbociclib + abemaciclib + ribociclib** (1× = 333/333/667 nM); conditions are **Untreated · PAR1x_P0 · PAR5x · P6_release**, where **P0 and P6 count hours after drug removal**, independent of passage. Dose is set per line for equivalent arrest — **1× arrests SKOV3, 5× arrests HEYA8** — so each line has one matched contrast, read as an arrest match rather than a dose response. ChIP was harvested at P0; **HEYA8 ChIP was done at 5×**, pairing it with the HEYA8 PAR5x RNA arm. Karl runs the full analysis in-house: RNA-seq (fastp→STAR→DESeq2) and ChIP-seq (bowtie2→SPP→IDR, the advisor's method) against Rb, p130, E2F1, E2F4, LIN54 — the Rb–E2F and DREAM repressive complexes. Pipelines in `code/ovarian/`, `code/chipseq/`. Dissertation Aim 1. First-author.

projects.name: The CRISPR paper
projects.status: palbociclib + nocodazole for improving CRISPR/HDR editing rates. Cell-cycle synchronization as a method for raising HDR efficiency: **palbociclib arrests, and transfection is timed 10–16 h after release to land in S phase**, with the nocodazole arm testing whether it adds anything beyond synchrony. Four lines — **HEYA8, HEPG2, HT1080, MDA-MB-231** plus **A549**, which is in the panel and in the writing: it arrested, then trickled back into the cell cycle without S-phase enrichment on release, so it received no ddPCR. That failure to synchronize is itself a result worth noting. Four conditions — **DF · P · N · P+N**. Two constructs — a **short ssODN** (3 silent edits) and a **long mScarlet PCR fragment** (35 bp homology arms) — plus gRNA-only, each with its own ddPCR assay (drop-off · silent-edit probe · mScarlet-junction). **Read out by ddPCR**; T7 endonuclease is a retired arm. Dissertation Aim 2. First-author, methods paper. *Conditions, assays, and replicate structure in full: `LAB_NOTEBOOK.md` Aug 12 2026.*

projects.name: The exosome paper (Bianca's)
projects.status: a **characterization paper about isolation methods** for small extracellular vesicles, by **TEM and AFM**. Bianca is first author. Karl's contribution is the **cargo/output characterization** of what the separation recovers — RNA isolation, library prep, and sequencing for MDA-MB-231 vs MCF10A (n=3 each), then the composition breakdown via a sequential small-RNA classification pipeline (rRNA→tRNA→miRNA→remainder→genome) in `code/exorna/`. **Karl's author position and figure allocation are undefined** — not settled by anyone. Authority runs through Bianca as first author and potentially **Dr. Caryn Heldt** (her other co-advisor); Goetsch is the less-involved co-advisor and asked *Karl* what his role was. Co-authored publication, outside the dissertation. *(The originally intended contribution was a miRNA comparison between the two lines; the available kits could not do it — see `RECEIPTS.md`.)*

projects.name: The CT gene paper
projects.status: how cancer/testis (CT) genes get **activated in the first place**: a coordinated germ-cell program, or stochastic noise? The field has largely studied CT *antigens* as immunotherapy targets and treats activation as stochastic; this asks the mechanistic question underneath. Built on two lab MS theses — **Clara Mosentine** (50 CT genes elevated in stage IV; most known CT genes activate *early*, not at metastasis) and **Zayne** (TCGA/GTEx/cell-line differential expression → a 28-gene mechanistic shortlist). Proposed discriminating test: compare testis-vs-normal, cancer-vs-normal, then (testis/normal) vs (cancer/normal); open threads include separating cancer-germline from cancer-testis, and comparison against embryo data. **Karl's contribution is conceptual, editorial, and figure-building — not pipeline work** (clarified Aug 10, 2026; the earlier "not computational" read too narrowly). Goetsch runs the pipeline and hands over the output. Karl sets the normal-tissue/cancer groupings — the anatomy and tissue-relevance call Goetsch, a *C. elegans* geneticist, is not positioned to make — builds the body map and the figures from that output, and writes the background: literature review; the semantics, etymology, and ontology of this niche's terminology; and the discussion (what "germline" means, and whether a soma-to-germline program in tumorigenesis is credible or stochastic).

projects.name: The dissertation
projects.status: three chapters. Aims 1 and 2 are the ovarian and CRISPR papers; **Aim 3 is the CT gene project**, entering as an in-progress aim with tables/visuals rather than a publication-ready chapter. Skeleton scaffolded with full section headers. **The bar:** a defensible dissertation plus two published papers, **venue open** — *"2 papers that I can get published literally wherever; it doesn't have to be Nature."* Target journals are chosen for scope-fit and review speed, and chosen **before** writing, since length limits set the figure count. Prestige-chasing is the thing most likely to cost a fall graduation.
